title: China's space dream
theme: space exploration, manned spaceflight, lunar exploration, national pride

section_a.question: What is one of the most spectacular endeavors of China's space exploration according to Para. 1?
options: Building a base on the far side of the moon
Building and operating China's first space station
Sending a probe to photograph the moon's far side
section_a.explanation: 第1段末句：All these astronauts have been training for one of the most spectacular endeavors of China's space exploration: building and operating China's first space station.

section_a.question: When was the PLA Astronaut Group established?
section_a.explanation: 第2段：1992 年立项并开始训练；1998 年这 14 名飞行员成为中国人民解放军航天员大队的创始成员（In 1998, they became the founding members of the PLA Astronaut Group.）。

section_a.question: What did it mean when Yang Liwei became the first Chinese person to go into space in the Shenzhou-5 manned mission?
options: China became the third country to send a man into space
China finished building its first space station
China became the first country to land on the moon
section_a.explanation: 第3段：making China the third country to send a man into space（使中国成为第三个把人送入太空的国家）。

section_a.question: What have the Chinese astronauts accomplished since Yang Liwei's momentous journey according to Para. 4?
options: They have lived on the Tiangong space station for a whole year
They have landed on the moon and brought back lunar samples
They have sent unmanned probes to Mars and to the moon's far side
They have performed scientific experiments and technological tests, undertaken extravehicular activities, and delivered a science lecture
section_a.explanation: 第4段：The astronauts have performed scientific experiments and technological tests, undertaken extravehicular activities, and even delivered a science lecture watched by tens of millions of students.

section_b.question: Why do we want to explore the moon according to the text?
options: To solve resource problems on earth.
To build a similar biosphere on the moon.
To peer into and explore the deep universe.
To learn more about the other side of the moon.
section_b.explanation: Text B 第2段：It's an ideal place to peer into the deep reaches of the universe. 其他三项在原文中都不是探月的理由。

section_b.question: Why is the far side of the moon also called the dark side?
options: It is covered by black rocks.
It is relatively unknown to us.
It is darker than the near side.
It is more dangerous than the near side.
section_b.explanation: 第3段：It's also called the dark side, although it's not darker than the near side. The word dark only shows how we feel about the unknown. 可见“dark”说的是我们对未知的感受，并非真得更暗。

section_b.question: Which of the following is the first-ever mission to photograph the moon's far side?
section_b.explanation: 第4段：Nobody had ever seen the moon's far side before the Soviet Union launched the Luna 3 probe in 1959. It was the first-ever mission to photograph the far side.

section_b.question: When did China join the lunar exploration club?
options: At the turn of the millennium.
section_b.explanation: 第5段：Since the turn of the millennium, more countries such as China, Japan, and India have joined the lunar exploration club. 2007 年是中国验证探月技术的年份，不是加入的时间。

section_c.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: China's space program aims at peaceful development for all
China plans to build a military base on the moon
China will stop cooperating with other countries in space
China spends more on space than on everyday needs
section_c.explanation: 全文主旨：中国以“和平发展”“人类命运共同体”为出发点探索太空，成果惠及全人类，并邀请各国参与合作（第2、6段）。

section_c.question: Which mission brought back samples of lunar rock?
section_c.explanation: 第1段：嫦娥五号（Chang'e-5）任务成功带回月岩样本；天问一号和祝融号负责火星探测。

section_c.question: According to Paragraph 3, space activities may help to ___.
options: replace international trade with space travel
ease shortages of energy and resources on earth
solve all social problems on earth
reduce the cost of building space stations
section_c.explanation: 第3段：太空活动有潜力解决能源和资源短缺、污染等问题，因此太空进步最终惠及所有人。

section_c.question: Why does the author mention the invention of the satellite?
options: To explain why satellites are expensive to launch
To prove that only rich nations can explore space
To show how space progress changes life on earth
To argue that globalization should be slowed down
section_c.explanation: 第4段：卫星等发明在推动全球化和互联互通方面价值巨大，说明太空成就改变了我们的生活方式。

section_a.title: No limit for China's astronauts in their space exploration endeavors
section_a.passage: China's space exploration had reached a new milestone by 2021, when three astronauts of Shenzhou-12 crew successfully docked at the Tiangong space station, worked there for months, and then safely returned to the earth. The three - Nie Haisheng, Liu Boming, and Tang Hongbo - were selected rigorously from the current active, qualified Chinese astronauts. All these astronauts have been training for one of the most spectacular endeavors of China's space exploration: building and operating China's first space station. It was back in 1992 that China approved a blueprint for her manned space program and began training astronauts. The first batch of astronauts was chosen from veteran pilots in the People's Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force who had at least 600 flight hours in fighter jets or attack aircraft. More than 1,500 pilots applied, and after rounds of most demanding tests, the number reduced sharply to 14. In 1998, they became the founding members of the PLA Astronaut Group. On October 15, 2003, Yang Liwei became the first Chinese person to go into space in the Shenzhou-5 manned mission, making China the third country to send a man into space. During his 600,000 km expedition, Yang simultaneously displayed the Chinese and UN flags to hundreds of millions of Chinese who were witnessing his feat on television, and said, “Make use of outer space peacefully and for the benefit of all humankind.” Since Yang's momentous journey, China has made a gigantic progress in space exploration, and more astronauts have been sent into orbit. The astronauts have performed scientific experiments and technological tests, undertaken extravehicular activities, and even delivered a science lecture watched by tens of millions of students. To achieve these accomplishments, though, the astronauts have endured countless rounds of training, tests, and drills, shedding sweat and owing an enormous debt to their families for their thorough understanding and continuous support. Once pilots are admitted to the astronaut team, they must immerse themselves in the study of about 60 subjects, including physics, astronautics, and astronomy. Normally, each of these subjects requires university students to take four-year courses, but the astronauts have just one year to complete their studies and must pass exams in every subject. During training, to simulate weightlessness, astronauts have to wear suits that weigh 160 kg and stay underwater for about four hours. They lose an average of 2 kg during each training session, and after a session they would be too exhausted to hold chopsticks. When conducting centrifuge training, astronauts must endure a force as much as eight times their own weight so that they will be able to resist the g-forces that severely restrict the ability to breathe during lift-off. None of the astronauts has pressed the emergency button to halt the program. The astronauts have also overcome hardships and difficulties during missions. Yang Liwei recalled that when Shenzhou-5 ascended toward the sky, a low-frequency oscillation made his internal organs vibrate violently, inflicting almost unbearable pain. He gritted his teeth and endured the pain because he was about to realize the nation's long-lasting dream of flying in space. During the Shenzhou-7 mission, Zhai Zhigang and Liu Boming discovered they were unable to open the spaceship's exit hatch. They decided to use a tool to force the hatch open despite the obvious safety risk. “We both knew what the other one was thinking at that very moment: We had to accomplish our mission and wave the Chinese flag in space, even though we realized that there would probably be no return trip for us,” Zhai said. Looking back at their experiences, the astronauts thought their struggles, sacrifices, and persistence were all worthwhile. It is awe-inspiring and unforgettable for the astronauts to observe the earth and the universe from space. “I saw the lights of cities on earth and lightning ripping through the night sky. From our orbit, I saw the darkness and emptiness of space, and I wondered where the boundary is between the sky and the stars. I will never forget those scenes,” said Liu Wang, who took part in the Shenzhou-9 mission. Jing Haipeng, who has taken part in several space missions, was awarded the August 1 Medal, the highest honor given to individual members of the Chinese PLA. Jing was both pleased and modest when he received the medal. For him, the honor and glory belong not only to the astronauts but also to tens of thousands of scientists, engineers, and workers who have played a role in the nation's manned space programs and contributed to sending the astronauts into space. The accomplishments of China's space exploration have become a source of pride and growing confidence in the nation, in addition to sparking patriotic sentiments in Chinese communities across the world. Wang Yaping, the female astronaut who delivered the science lecture from space, felt overwhelmed by the number of boys and girls who wrote to her upon her return. She had never imagined that her teaching could trigger off so many dreams and aspirations. Yang Liwei recalled that during a visit to New York, a Chinese-American held his hands and tearfully told him that the nation's achievements in space reflected the fact that “our motherland has risen”, which gave Chinese people living overseas more courage and strength. The bravery, wisdom, and commitment the Chinese astronauts embody will definitely inspire numerous young people to join the lofty cause and set space as the stage to realize their ambitions and the dream of national rejuvenation. There is no limit to the vast universe or to China's space exploration endeavors.

section_b.title: Chang'e-4 kicked off a new space odyssey
section_b.passage: No wind blows and no rain falls there. Only crashing meteorites occasionally disrupt the stillness. The desolate landscape on the moon's far side has waited billions of years to see the first-ever soft landing of a visitor from the earth - Chang'e-4 from China. As the nearest heavenly body, the moon has fascinated humankind since we first gazed at the sky. The silver disc in the sky is always a captivating theme in our legends, myths, and dreams. Its ever-changing face has inspired ambitious aspirations. We admire its beauty from the earth, so why are we so eager to reach the moon? It's an ideal place to peer into the deep reaches of the universe. It inspires our imaginations and dreams of space travel. The moon and the earth share a similar “childhood”, yet traces of the remote past on earth have been erased by geological activities. Exploration of the moon might provide some insights into the early history of the earth. But due to the tidal locking effect, we only get to see one side of the moon from the earth, and the far side remains a mystery. It's also called the dark side, although it's not darker than the near side. The word dark only shows how we feel about the unknown. Nobody had ever seen the moon's far side before the Soviet Union launched the Luna 3 probe in 1959. It was the first-ever mission to photograph the far side. The United States Apollo 8 mission sent three astronauts around the moon in 1968, the first time humans saw the moon's far side with their own eyes. Now China sent the first-ever probe to soft-land and rove on the far side, which has deepened our understanding of the moon, the earth, and the universe. Between the 1950s and 1970s, the United States and the Soviet Union raced against each other in early lunar exploration. After a lull, new interest was triggered in the 1990s when scientists found there might be water on the moon. Since the turn of the millennium, more countries such as China, Japan, and India have joined the lunar exploration club. To date, the world has launched over 100 manned or unmanned missions to the moon. Flying to the moon has been a dream of the Chinese since ancient times. The moon has long been a major theme in Chinese poems, music, and paintings, with artists and writers using the moon to express their emotions and thoughts about the universe. Since the 1990s, Chinese scientists and engineers have endeavored to make the dream a reality. China announced in 2000 that its space planning agenda contained preparatory research about lunar exploration. It officially began the lunar exploration program in 2004, with the aim of orbiting and landing on the moon, and bringing samples back to the earth. The program was named after the moon goddess Chang'e, who, in Chinese mythology, lived on the moon and was accompanied by the Jade Rabbit. Although China is a latecomer in lunar exploration, its program has made many achievements in a few expeditions. The country verified its lunar probe technologies in 2007 with the successful launch of Chang'e-1, the first spacecraft stemming from the program. In 2013 Chang'e-3 accomplished China's first soft-landing on the moon, which was the first man-made craft to achieve this goal in nearly four decades. After Chang'e-3's accomplishment, Chinese space experts aimed high to make the Chang'e-4 mission more innovative and challenging: to realize the first-ever soft-landing on the far side of the moon. In order to achieve that goal, China launched a relay satellite, named Queqiao (Magpie Bridge) after an ancient legend, to set up a communication link between the earth and the moon's far side. Chinese space experts also overcame difficulties with the rugged terrain on the far side, making the probe land on the moon with high precision. The Chang'e-4 mission carried instruments that had been developed by scientists from Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, and Saudi Arabia, providing more opportunities for the world's scientists and combining human wisdom to explore the universe. Now China is drawing up plans to explore the moon's polar regions and inviting other countries to join in further expeditions. “I think one of the beauties of space science is that we do cooperate internationally. Space science to me is something important, also as a message of peace worldwide,” said a German professor in the program. The probe took some live species like cotton and potato to the lifeless environment to form a mini biosphere, which is expected to produce the first flower on the moon. Engineers also plan to get data by constantly measuring temperatures on the surface of the moon. From robotic to manned missions, from short- to long-term, China's lunar exploration will go deeper. The Chinese will leave their footprints on the surface of the moon in the foreseeable future. Exploring the moon has inspired scientists and engineers, fascinated young and old, and motivated young people to pursue scientific careers, not only in space but also in the depths of the ocean or in the nucleus of an atom. Reaching the moon, the first outpost in deep space, is just the beginning of our space odyssey.

section_c.title: China aims for peaceful use of space exploration
section_c.passage: Over the past few years, China has made great achievements and experienced a number of breakthroughs pertaining to outer space. The Chang'e-5 mission successfully brought back samples of lunar rock. The core module of Tiangong, the space station, was launched and astronauts were sent up there. China also became just the second nation to land a rover on Mars with the Tianwen-1 mission and Zhurong probe. Furthermore, China and Russia have released a joint road map for building the International Lunar Research Station, which will be the first structures built on the moon, by 2035. Long before the modern era, Chinese culture and tradition attached great importance to the heavens and the moon, and from here emerged many of the world's earliest astronomers and cosmologists. China's vision for the exploration of outer space should be understood through the lens of its economic strategy for “peaceful development” and “a global community of shared future” for the good of humankind. China has a nonmilitary view of space exploration and sees advances in science as a means for accelerating global prosperity and economic development. Since the 20th century, outer space has been the newest frontier of humankind, and understanding it and knowing how to use it productively are crucial for humanity. The advancement of space-related activities has the potential to overcome many problems on earth, including shortages of energy and resources as well as pollution. As a consequence, progress made in space is ultimately progress in the name of all, and serves to benefit all. Each civil feat in space subsequently transforms the way we live, even if we do not realize it. The achievements of the 20th century transformed our world in communications and expanded our capability to understand ourselves. The invention of the satellite and similar resources has been invaluable in promoting globalization and interconnectivity. As a result, the Tiangong space station and the planned International Lunar Research Station will aim to shape the future of humanity accordingly, by expanding the scope of knowledge to new levels. The Chinese endeavor is not a zero-sum game; China invites all countries to participate in its projects as a peaceful initiative and to help shape humanity's future. China will pursue the path of peaceful development in space with a view to the moon, Mars, and beyond.

questions.question: What do astronauts have to do to simulate weightlessness during training?
options: Spend eight hours a day in a centrifuge
Wear suits that weigh 160 kg and stay underwater for about four hours
Train inside a spaceship orbiting the earth
Hold chopsticks for hours after every session
questions.explanation: 第7段：to simulate weightlessness, astronauts have to wear suits that weigh 160 kg and stay underwater for about four hours。

questions.question: What did Zhai Zhigang and Liu Boming decide to do when they discovered they were unable to open the spaceship's exit hatch?
options: They decided to give up the mission and return to the earth
They decided to ask the ground control to send a new hatch
They decided to use a tool to force the hatch open despite the safety risk
They decided to wait until the hatch opened by itself
questions.explanation: 第8段：They decided to use a tool to force the hatch open despite the obvious safety risk。

questions.question: What are the impacts that the accomplishments of China's space exploration have on the Chinese at home and abroad?
options: They have made young Chinese lose interest in science
They have replaced traditional Chinese culture with space technology
They have benefited only the scientists and engineers working in the program
They have become a source of pride and growing confidence at home and sparked patriotic sentiments in Chinese communities abroad
questions.explanation: 第11段：The accomplishments ... have become a source of pride and growing confidence in the nation, in addition to sparking patriotic sentiments in Chinese communities across the world.

questions.question: What are the qualities the Chinese astronauts embody?
questions.explanation: 第12段：The bravery, wisdom, and commitment the Chinese astronauts embody will definitely inspire numerous young people ...

questions.question: All these industries have ______ the decline and in some cases reversed it by innovations of their own.
questions.explanation: halt 意为“（使）停止”，halt the decline 指“遏止下滑”；embody（体现）、simulate（模拟）、ascend（上升）均不合搭配。

questions.question: The city has recently devised a series of strategies mapping out a(n) ______ for the city's development.
questions.explanation: blueprint 指“蓝图、规划”，map out a blueprint for ... development 是常用搭配；boundary（边界）、milestone（里程碑）、oscillation（摆动）都不能与 map out 搭配表示“规划”。

questions.question: Research laboratories could ______ environmental conditions surrounding historical sites to help researchers with their cultural heritage protection endeavors.
questions.explanation: simulate 意为“模拟”，simulate environmental conditions 即“模拟环境条件”，符合实验室研究的语境。

questions.question: My phone ______ in my pocket while I was walking around the mall.
questions.explanation: vibrate 指“振动”，手机在口袋里振动用 vibrated；其余三词分别表示停止、体现、模拟，均不能描述手机。

questions.question: This meeting proved to be a very important ______ for the development of the program.
questions.explanation: milestone 指“里程碑、重大事件”，an important milestone for the development of ... 表示“项目发展的重要里程碑”。

questions.question: The drought has ______ a direct agricultural economic loss of 952 million dollars in that area.
questions.explanation: inflict 意为“使遭受（不愉快的事）”，inflict a loss on ... 指“造成损失”；此处 inflict a direct agricultural economic loss 表示“造成直接农业经济损失”。

It helped humans see the moon's far side with their own eyes for the first time.
It carried instruments developed by foreign scientists from Japan and Germany.
questions.explanation: 第8段：to realize the first-ever soft-landing on the far side of the moon；第4段也说 Now China sent the first-ever probe to soft-land and rove on the far side。“fresh flowers”与原文 cotton and potato 不符；C 项是 Apollo 8 宇航员首次用肉眼看到；D 项国家名单错误。

questions.question: The successful re-entry and landing of the Chang'e-5 probe has enabled China to obtain its first lunar samples, marking ______ progress in lunar and planetary research.
questions.explanation: gigantic progress 意为“巨大进步”，与“首次获得月球样品”这一重大成果匹配；continuous（持续的）、momentary（短暂的）都不表示程度之大。

questions.question: With this achievement, China has ______ a new milestone in the space domain.
questions.explanation: reach a milestone 是固定搭配，意为“达到一个里程碑”；deepen（加深）、accomplish（完成）不能与 milestone 搭配。

questions.question: The primary goal of Chang'e-5 was to bring back samples from the moon's surface. This will ______ our understanding of the state, temperature, and material content of the moon.
questions.explanation: deepen our understanding 意为“加深我们的理解”，与 understanding 构成固定搭配；reach、accomplish、disrupt 均不与 understanding 搭配。

questions.question: No matter how far China goes into space, it always aims at ______ its original mission - revealing the secrets of the universe and providing great continuous support for humanity's peaceful use of space.
questions.explanation: accomplish one's mission 意为“完成使命”，aime at accomplishing its original mission 表示“以完成其最初使命为目标”。

questions.question: No matter how far China goes into space, it always aims at accomplishing its original mission - revealing the secrets of the universe and providing great ______ support for humanity's peaceful use of space.
questions.explanation: continuous support 意为“持续的支持”，与 providing ... support for humanity's peaceful use of space 搭配；momentary（短暂的）与语义相反。

sentences.zh: 实现中华民族伟大复兴是近代以来中国人民最伟大的梦想，我们称之为“中国梦”，其基本内涵是实现国家富强、民族振兴、人民幸福。
sentences.en_reference: To realize the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation has been the greatest dream of the Chinese people since modern times. We call it the “Chinese Dream”, whose essential meaning is to build a prosperous and strong country, to rejuvenate the nation, and to bring happiness to the people.

sentences.zh: 每个中国人都是中国梦的参与者和创造者。
sentences.en_reference: Every Chinese is a participant in and a creator of the Chinese Dream.

sentences.zh: 我们要把自己的前途与国家的命运紧紧相连。
sentences.en_reference: We should link our own future closely with the destiny of our country.

sentences.zh: 中国梦是民族的梦，也是每个中国人的梦。
sentences.en_reference: The Chinese Dream is the dream of the nation, and it is also the dream of every Chinese.

sentences.zh: 我们应坚定信心、同心同德，为全面推进中华民族伟大复兴而团结奋斗。
sentences.en_reference: We should have firm confidence, work with one heart and one mind, and strive in unity to advance the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation in all respects.

writing.prompt: Write an essay of no less than 140 words on one of the following topics: “Curiosity and scientific breakthroughs” (an outline is given), “Procrastination is a bad habit”, or “Exploring the space for the benefit of all humankind”. Support your point with sufficient examples that are specific and typical, interesting and relevant, and arrange them in a clear order.
outline: Introduction: State the thesis that curiosity is the secret to scientific breakthroughs.
Body 1: Curiosity sparks questions that matter in scientific discovery - the example of Li Siguang and the Quaternary Glacial Theory of China.
Body 2: Curiosity gives people the persistence to keep looking for discoveries - the examples of Michael Faraday and Tu Youyou.
Conclusion: Curiosity plays a key role in important scientific breakthroughs.
